title: Do electricians in Australia have to do CPD to renew their licence?
description: Mandatory CPD for Victorian electrical licences (8 hour skills maintenance, skills development from 2028) compared with Queensland skills maintenance.
shortAnswer: It depends on the state. Victoria has mandatory continuing professional development (CPD) for electrical licences: since July 1, 2023 every renewal requires 8 hours of Energy Safe Victoria skills maintenance training in the two years before renewal, and from July 1, 2028 most licence holders also need 8 hours of skills development. Queensland requires evidence of skills maintenance within two years of renewal, through an RTO course or an online assessment.
keyTakeaways: Energy Safe Victoria (ESV) describes its program as Victoria's first CPD program for the electrical trades. Skills maintenance has been required for all electrical licence renewals after July 1, 2023.
Victorian skills maintenance is about eight hours of in person training per licence class, completed within the two years before renewal. There is no exam.

Skills development, 8 hours of new learning per person per 5 year cycle, becomes a renewal requirement from July 1, 2028 for electricians, supervised electricians, licensed electrical inspectors and switchgear workers.

Queensland's Electrical Safety Office requires licence holders to show skills maintained in the last two years in electrical safety legislation, risk management and testing, by an RTO course or an online self paced assessment.
The NSW Building Commission CPD page lists builders, swimming pool builders, certifiers, design and building practitioners and engineers, but not electricians.
regulator: Energy Safe Victoria (ESV) for Victorian electrical licences; Electrical Safety Office, Office of Industrial Relations, for Queensland electrical work licences

sections.heading: Which Australian states require CPD for electricians?

blocks.text: Victoria is the clearest case: [Energy Safe Victoria](https://www.energysafe.vic.gov.au/licensing/cpd-introduction) runs a mandatory CPD program, and states that "CPD is required for all electrical licence renewals after 1 July 2023". Queensland does not call its scheme CPD, but the Electrical Safety Office makes evidence of recent skills maintenance a condition of renewing an electrical work licence.

In New South Wales, the [Building Commission NSW CPD page](https://www.nsw.gov.au/business-and-economy/licences-and-credentials/building-and-trade-licences-and-registrations/continuing-professional-development) covers residential and swimming pool builders, certifiers, design and building practitioners and professional engineers. Electrical licences are not among them. Other jurisdictions were not reviewed for this page, so this is not a complete national list.

blocks.title: Currency
blocks.text: This page reflects Energy Safe Victoria and Queensland Electrical Safety Office guidance as at November 2026. Victoria's skills development requirement has not yet commenced; it applies to renewals from July 1, 2028.

sections.heading: Why did Victoria make CPD mandatory for electrical licences?

blocks.text: ESV's FAQ explains that electrical licences are renewed every 5 years for a fee and that historically there was "no mandatory ongoing training required, or any proof of ongoing competence". It cites research that licence holders may not be aware of revisions to standards and may have forgotten mandatory testing requirements in legislation.

ESV frames the program around three Cs: currency, competency and complacency. Course content was created by Future Energy Skills, a not for profit organization led by the Electrical Trades Union and the National Electrical and Communications Association, under an industry committee that also includes ESV and the Institute of Electrical Inspectors. ESV notes that the Victorian Government committed that no licence holder would pay for their course in the first round of renewals.

sections.heading: What does Victorian skills maintenance involve?

blocks.text: [Skills maintenance](https://www.energysafe.vic.gov.au/licensing/continuing-professional-development/skills-maintenance) is refresher training required for all electrical licences. It takes a total of eight hours of in person training at a specialist training center or TAFE, and must be completed within the two years before the licence renewal is due. Holders of more than one licence class complete a course for each class.

items: Electricians, supervised electricians, restricted and switchgear licence holders: about 60% hands on and 40% theory, covering licence holder responsibilities, current regulations and standards, safe isolation and mandatory testing.
Licensed electrical inspectors: a 4 hour core module plus a 4 hour module for each inspector class (G, H, M, V and RE).
Lineworkers and cable jointers: modules for classes C, D, T and R covering legislated responsibilities, equipotential zones, earthing and radio frequency awareness.
There is no exam. ESV says the trainer may highlight areas where skills could be improved.

blocks.text: Licences can be renewed up to 90 days before expiry, through ESVConnect. A licence holder who cannot finish the course in time can request an extension during the renewal application. If granted, ESV will typically renew for the usual 5 years with a condition to complete the course within up to 12 months, and may suspend or cancel the licence if that condition is not met. Living in a remote part of Victoria or financial hardship are generally not accepted grounds.

sections.heading: What changes in 2028 with skills development?

blocks.text: From July 1, 2028, renewals for electricians, supervised electricians, licensed electrical inspectors and switchgear workers will need [skills development](https://www.energysafe.vic.gov.au/licensing/continuing-professional-development/skills-development) as well as skills maintenance. Skills development is 8 hours of training in a new or emerging area, counted per person rather than per licence, and can be done at any time in the 5 years before renewal.

ESV accepts training in three categories: electrical industry technical training; non technical electrical industry training in safety or business skills; and mental health and wellbeing, including diversity and inclusion. Training may be accredited, such as a unit of competency from an RTO regulated by ASQA, the Victorian Registration and Qualifications Authority or the Western Australian Training Accreditation Council, or a university course, or non accredited. Evidence is subject to audit.

sections.heading: How does Queensland's skills maintenance rule compare?

blocks.text: Queensland's requirement is narrower but also mandatory. The Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) makes competence in the work authorized by the licence a renewal criterion, and the [Electrical Safety Office](https://www.worksafe.qld.gov.au/licensing-and-registrations/electrical-training/skills-maintenance-courses) requires licence holders to prove at renewal that they have kept skills and knowledge current in three areas: electrical safety legislation, risk management, and testing. Only skills maintained in the last two years count.

Queensland licence holders can meet this through an RTO course or a free online self paced skills maintenance assessment, which requires identity verification through Digital ID (an alternative assessment can be arranged). Queensland also requires current rescue and resuscitation competence at renewal, covered on the [Queensland CPR and rescue training page](/regulations/queensland-electrical-worker-annual-cpr-and-rescue-training).

sections.heading: What should an employer track for electrical licence CPD?

blocks.text: The licence holder carries the CPD obligation, but an employer whose workers lose their licence loses the ability to deploy them. The practical controls are a renewal date per licence class, the date skills maintenance was completed for each class, and from 2028 in Victoria, the skills development hours and category for each person.

The guide on [setting mandatory refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles) explains how to schedule rolling windows like these so a renewal is never the first time the gap is noticed.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry maps CPD content to the knowledge points it refreshes, such as isolation, mandatory testing and regulatory changes, so internal toolbox training and external CPD courses can be seen against the same framework. That helps an employer decide which in house topics complement, rather than duplicate, the ESV or ESO requirement. See how this applies to [energy and resources organizations](/industries/energy-resources).

faqs.q: Is there an age exemption from Victorian electrical CPD?
faqs.a: No. ESV states there are no age restrictions for doing the training and no exemptions based on age. Anyone who wants to renew a Victorian electrical licence must be registered with ESVConnect and complete the required CPD training.

faqs.q: Do I need separate CPD for each Victorian licence class I hold?
faqs.a: For skills maintenance, yes: a course is required for each licence class, with little duplication between courses. Skills development is counted per person, so it is met once every 5 year cycle regardless of how many classes are held.

faqs.q: Can a Victorian electrician working interstate get an extension?
faqs.a: Living or working outside Victoria is listed as a possible ground for a first extension, but ESV says it is generally not adequate grounds for a further extension. ESV suggests either obtaining the equivalent licence in the other state or completing the skills maintenance course.

faqs.q: What happens if my Victorian licence expires before I do the CPD?
faqs.a: ESV's FAQ says CPD skills maintenance must be completed before reinstating the licence, although an extension can be requested as part of the application. Doing electrical work without a current licence is unlawful.
